answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a prism as the anchor of the cost. A terrace stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a vault holds the rep...
